questions.question: A previously healthy adult develops fulminant sepsis with disseminated intravascular coagulation 4 days after a dog bite. Which zoonotic pathogen should be strongly suspected, and what microbiologic characteristic commonly delays culture-based diagnosis?

In the initial phase of this case, what clinical and laboratory features supported sepsis-associated DIC rather than primary thrombotic microangiopathy, and why can the two processes be difficult to distinguish early?

After the patient’s sepsis and coagulopathy began improving, she developed a new fall in hemoglobin, persistent thrombocytopenia, elevated LDH, undetectable haptoglobin, and 15%–20% schistocytes. What is the most important next diagnostic framework for this syndrome, and which major thrombotic microangiopathies must be rapidly differentiated in an adult with AKI?

How do ADAMTS13 activity testing and Shiga toxin testing help distinguish TTP, STEC-HUS, and complement-mediated HUS in an adult with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury?

This patient initially had a positive direct antiglobulin test for IgG, but corticosteroids did not improve the hemolysis and repeat testing became negative. What features argue against autoimmune hemolytic anemia and instead support thrombotic microangiopathy as the cause of hemolysis?

Why do normal C3 and C4 levels not exclude complement-mediated HUS, and what is the underlying pathophysiologic mechanism by which infection can trigger this disorder even in the absence of an identified pathogenic complement gene variant?
What renal biopsy findings are most consistent with thrombotic microangiopathy in this case, and how can biopsy help when the diagnosis remains uncertain after laboratory evaluation?

Why is plasma exchange often started empirically in adults presenting with thrombotic microangiopathy while ADAMTS13 results are pending, and why is its role different in complement-mediated HUS than in TTP?

What factors should guide the timing of eculizumab initiation in a patient with suspected complement-mediated HUS who recently had documented Capnocytophaga bacteremia, and what infection-prevention measures are required when starting terminal complement blockade?
